messages:
emma: FYI sampleapp CI started failing after the latest autogen stubs merge. both mypy and pyright complain about mutual TypedDict imports. quick log below.

emma: repro (generated files):
```py
# models/order.py (autogen stub)
from typing import TypedDict
from .customer import CustomerDict

class OrderDict(TypedDict):
    id: str
    customer: CustomerDict

# models/customer.py (autogen stub)
from typing import TypedDict
from .order import OrderDict

class CustomerDict(TypedDict):
    id: str
    last_order: OrderDict
```

riley: ugh. circular TypedDicts bite hard. two ways we've mitigated before: emit `from __future__ import annotations` in stubs, or guard cross-module type imports under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`.

oz: note pyright in editor often still flags unresolved imports even with future annotations. pyright's strict import resolution doesn't always get quieted.

emma: i tried a local patch: i generated a tiny runtime shim `models/_runtime.py` with lightweight dataclasses (or simple alias vars) so runtime imports resolve, then keep full typing in `models/__init__.pyi` or stub files. that keeps runtime behavior stable while avoiding circular runtime imports.

ingrid: interesting. so runtime shim provides real objects for `from models import CustomerDict` at runtime, but types remain in .pyi stubs?

emma: exactly. example shim:````py
# models/_runtime.py
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Customer:
    id: str
    # last_order left as Any to avoid runtime cycle
    last_order: object | None = None
````
then we export simple names in `models/__init__.py` and keep `models/*.pyi` for strong typing.

riley: that seems pragmatic. generator could emit a small runtime shim whenever there are inter-model cycles, or when a user opts in via a flag. avoid surprising consumers who import at runtime.

oz: for magic methods we discussed before: `__aenter__` and `__iter__` in generated async helpers should use `-> Any` (or string forward refs) so importing the client doesn't force loading model modules. prefer Any for dunders.

ingrid: +1. also propose generator flag `--runtime-shim=auto|none|dataclass` default `auto` which creates minimal runtime objects only if cycles detected. and `--emit-pyi` to control whether we emit .pyi stubs or inline typing in .py files.

emma: also found pyright config helpful: adding a pyrightconfig.json with `pythonVersion: 3.11` and `typeCheckingMode: "basic"` can reduce false positives in editor mode for some teams. we should document that in SDK integration notes.

riley: we should add CI tests in generator upstream: a small matrix that generates both shim+pyi and no-shim variants, then run mypy and pyright against a repo with mutual models. catch regressions early.

oz: for immediate mitigation in sampleapp: vendor the patched stubs into the repo (temporary), or pin generator to previous tag. both are quick but ugly. better to ship generator PR soon.

emma: i'll open a generator PR proposing: 1) detect cycles and emit runtime shims; 2) default `from __future__ import annotations` in emitted stubs for py>=3.10; 3) annotate magic dunders with `Any`; 4) add CI matrix for mypy+pyright combos.

ingrid: please add a small note in the changelog and the SDK upgrade guide explaining the shim behavior and the opt-out flags so integrators know what to expect. also add a sample pyrightconfig snippet.

emma: will do. tagging @ingrid on the PR when ready. opening in ~1hr.

ci-bot: CI: sampleapp/mypy job failed -> https://ci.internal/2345/build/10101 (mypy errors) :eyes:

riley: thanks emma. once the PR lands we should run a canary bump in the sampleapp repo to validate before wide rollout. :thumbsup:
